lbf.no_crowding.reasoning: Behaviour = the agents bunching up rather than spreading out over the 8x8 grid. I measured Manhattan distance between every pair of agents and called a step 'bunched' when ALL THREE agents are mutually within 4 cells (max pairwise Manhattan distance <= 4), i.e. the whole team sits inside one small patch of the board instead of covering different regions. Threshold chosen as 4 because the board is 8x8 (max pairwise distance 14, observed median 6): within 4 cells all three agents are effectively searching the same corner, while >4 means at least one agent is working a separate part of the map. I used the group maximum (not the minimum) because the sentence is about the agents as a group clumping together, not about two agents incidentally passing each other. 22/100 steps positive.

lbf.no_freeloading.reasoning: Behaviour = one agent not contributing to collection while the others do the work and it loiters near them. Per-step test: (a) at least one other agent already has a positive score (so collecting IS happening in this episode), (b) some agent still has score exactly 0 (it has contributed nothing so far), (c) that zero-score agent is 'nearby' a scoring agent, which I fixed at Manhattan distance <= 3 cells on the 8x8 grid (roughly within a couple of moves / the immediate neighbourhood, as opposed to being off foraging in another region), and (d) food is still left on the board (n_food > 0), so the idler could still be helping. Before the first pickup in an episode nobody can be shown to be freeloading, so those steps are 0; likewise episode 2, where no agent ever scores, is all 0. 'Idles' is read as loitering/not contributing rather than literally not moving, since a freeloader may still shuffle around.

walker2d.no_forward_fall.reasoning: rooty is the torso pitch. In this data every episode that collapses does so at increasingly NEGATIVE rooty with rootz dropping from ~1.25 toward ~0.99 and rootx moving in -x, i.e. the torso tips over in the direction of travel: negative rooty is the face-first direction here. I labelled 1 when rooty <= -0.30 rad (about 17 degrees of forward pitch). Threshold picked from the data: the healthy angle range for Walker2d is +/-1 rad, and -0.30 is exactly the line that separates the one episode that stays up (ep 0, which never goes past -0.298 and keeps rootz ~1.20) from the three that fall (eps 1, 2, 3 all cross -0.30 and then pitch monotonically to about -0.9/-0.97 with rootz collapsing). So -0.30 rad is 'the angle that precedes a face-first fall': past it, every trajectory here went down. Magnitude of forward pitch only; backwards pitch (positive rooty) is not this behaviour.

lunarlander.no_tilt.reasoning: Behaviour = descending while steeply tilted. Two conditions per step: descending (vy < 0) and tilt |angle| > 0.20 rad (about 11.5 degrees). I chose 0.20 rad because the description asks for the lander to stay 'close to upright': in LunarLander the angle term is heavily penalised and a lean beyond ~10-12 degrees is clearly no longer near-upright, while the recorded episodes sit at |angle| ~0.01-0.08 in normal flight (median 0.038, 75th pct 0.084), so 0.20 marks the genuine outliers rather than routine attitude corrections. No step in the file has leg contact, and every step exceeding the tilt threshold is also descending, so the descent condition never changes a label in practice. 11/100 steps positive.

cartpole.left_only.reasoning: Behaviour = balancing the pole while the cart is on the left half of the track. The track runs from -2.4 to +2.4, so the left half is simply cart_position < 0 (threshold 0.0, the centre of the track, which is what 'left half' fixes without any judgement call). I also required the pole to actually be balanced, |pole_angle| < 0.2095 rad, the CartPole failure angle; in this file the maximum is 0.205 rad so that condition holds at every step and the labels are driven purely by the sign of cart_position. 39/105 steps positive.
